issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking protection from eviction for rent default must pay or tender rent regularly during the suit or appeal, and a court cannot treat persistent payment at irregular intervals as substantial compliance merely because arrears are cleared before judgment.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession on the ground of rent default. The matter proceeded to an appeal that remained pending for about 40 months.
Rent was payable monthly, but the tenant deposited it only 16 times during the appeal, at intervals ranging from two to four months, rather than paying it monthly as it fell due or in advance.
The tenant’s final rent payment was made after final arguments, and the arrears had been cleared by the time judgment was pronounced.
issues.conclusion: The requirement to pay or tender rent regularly during the suit or appeal is mandatory. Because the tenant paid at persistently irregular intervals, the tenant was not entitled to protection from eviction; the appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and a decree for possession was passed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 requires strict compliance with its conditions and creates no discretionary jurisdiction to excuse non-compliance. “Regularly” requires payment or tender with reasonable punctuality and substantial proximity to the intervals at which rent falls due. For monthly rent, the tenant must pay or tender it every month as it falls due or in advance; persistent payments at intervals of two, three, or four months are not substantial compliance, even if arrears are cleared before judgment. The Court relied on Ganpat Ladha v. Sashikant Vishnu Shinde, which followed Shah Dhansukhlal Chagganlal and Harbanslal Jagmohandas v. Prabhudas Shivlal.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought possession because the tenant had defaulted in paying rent, and the matter was before a court in the suit or an appeal.
predicates.tenant_paid_at_persistently_irregular_in: The tenant paid or tendered rent repeatedly at intervals that did not substantially conform to the monthly due sequence, rather than paying monthly as rent fell due or in advance.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession for rent default in a suit or appeal, rent is due monthly, and the tenant repeatedly pays at intervals that do not substantially conform to the monthly due sequence, the tenant is not entitled to protection from eviction.
